title: Normalized derived invariants through an open normal subgroup
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on a small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$ use $\mathcal A_P(A)$, the category of internal $A$-modules with $A$-linear condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $G,L$ be profinite groups and $K\triangleleft G$ an open normal subgroup; put $Q=G/K$, with its finite discrete topology. Inflation along $G\times L\to Q\times L$ is exact and has a right adjoint $T$ given by $K$-fixed sections, with residual $Q\times L$-action. The categories involved are Grothendieck abelian. Restriction of actions and forgetting actions are exact. Form ordinary total right derived functors by K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $U_{Q\times L}$ for forgetting the $Q\times L$-action and $\operatorname{Res}_K$ for restriction of a $G\times L$-action along $k\mapsto(k,1)$. There are natural isomorphisms
$$D(U_{Q\times L})\,RT(N)\cong R\Gamma_K(\operatorname{Res}_K N),\qquad
c_N:R\Gamma_{G\times L}(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(RT(N))$$
for $N\in D(\mathcal A_{G\times L}(A))$. The second is the derived composition comparison for the identity of invariant submodules $N^{G\times L}=(N^K)^{Q\times L}$ and the normalized inflation adjunctions, whose transposes restrict codomain to invariants and whose inverse transposes compose with the invariant inclusion.

For a module $N$ in degree zero let $\eta_N:T(N)[0]\to RT(N[0])$ be the canonical resolution map. Its underlying map under the first comparison is the usual map from $K$-invariants into derived $K$-invariants. The inflation map $\operatorname{inf}_N:R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(T(N)[0])\to R\Gamma_{G\times L}(N[0])$ satisfies
$$c_N\operatorname{inf}_N=R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N).$$
These comparisons and this equation are natural in equivariant module maps and in continuous homomorphisms $L'\to L$. For successive quotient projections they respect composition: the derived inflation attached to the composite projection and composite invariant inclusion is the composite of the two derived inflations. They commute with restriction of coefficients along every condensed ring map $A\to A'$ and the derived coefficient transformations induced by equivariant maps $N\to\operatorname{Res}N'$; these transformations are obtained by deriving the equality of invariants with scalar restriction. For $K=1$, the map $\eta_N$ and the comparisons are the identity under the evident identifications.
